thesis: Both sides establish continued monetisation and slower shareholder conversion, but neither prices recurring incentives, legal costs and owner cash. Neutral preserves broad payment growth while declining a premium-value conclusion. Visa's investment thesis concerns network economics rather than bank spreads.
strongest_counterexample: Net revenue grew14% despite incentive offsets, GAAP profit still grew7%, payment volumes10% and cross-border excluding Europe12%, proving continued real monetisation.
invalidation_conditions: A subsequent comparable quarter reports GAAP net-income growth at least equal to net-revenue growth with positive reconciled owner cash after recurring legal/incentive costs, resolving the conversion gap.
Comparable net-revenue or GAAP earnings growth at or below zero would invalidate the retained positive-monetisation counterweight.
evidence_gaps: Recurring incentives, litigation and severance treatment.
FCF, net debt and owner-cash valuation.
decisive_factors: 31.46x vendor reference lacks matched value; muted MACD and weak volume.
